key: After power-up, one valve stayed open.
report:
Got a gas release at Coulee Creek station near 100 Mile House. Found it at 0830 today.

Maintenance crew was swapping a compressor control panel. After power-up, one valve stayed open. Sweet gas vented through the relief line. Station meter logged 159,600 m³ released, exact number.

Same panel failed last month. After power-up, the controller lost comms and the station tripped. Tech said comms card was flaky.

Shut in the station, isolated the panel. New card on order, should be here tomorrow.

key: Valve was tagged "closed" but the handle was about 1/4 turn off seat.
report:
Subject: gas release at Compressor Station 4

Just rolled up to Station 4 around 1530 for the quarterly valve grease job. At 1538 I caught a sweet gas smell near the suction scrubber skid. Walked the lines, found the 3-inch vent on the scrubber discharge was open. Valve was tagged "closed" but the handle was about 1/4 turn off seat. No flowmeter on the vent so no number on volume.

Same vent was found open on this skid last October. Valve handle was wide open and the tag was missing.

Compressor was running the whole time, no trip. Secured the valve and called it in. Site's stable now.

- L. Chen, Field Op

key: Landed wrong, ended up with a broken femur.
report:
Hey,

Got a call from site near Wonowon at around 16:00 today—contractor crew hit a snag. One of the guys, name not given yet, took a bad fall off a Cat. Landed wrong, ended up with a broken femur. They had him on a backboard and airlifted to hospital right away. No product release, line's still tight, just the injury.

Same crew had a guy fall off a Cat last spring too. Landed wrong, ended up with a sprained wrist.

Not sure what they were doing exactly—supervisor just said "construction work". Will follow up if more comes in.

—Raj, Control Room

key: Heat discoloration on the separator shell and some wiring harness melted off the scrubber control panel.
report:
Got a call from the night shift at Sundre station—fire on east compressor pad around 21:00 May 26. Crew saw flames, pulled the E-stop, called 911. Local FD showed up, knocked it down quick. Looked like the inlet scrubber skid caught. Heat discoloration on the separator shell and some wiring harness melted off the scrubber control panel. No product hit the fire, everything stayed inside pipe. Still running a temp line through the unit to keep downstream pressure up; will need to swap the scrubber ASAP.

Same pad had a small fire in 2024 too. Only scorch marks on the drip trays.

—J. Delgado, Area Supervisor

key: Estimated volume released is about 36,000 m³.
report:
Got a call from the landowner near Temagami, Ontario, on 2026-07-09 around 18:12. They reported a gas release at Northline Gas Transmission Ltd.'s compression station. Patrol team headed there to check it out.

Upon arrival, we confirmed a leak. The product released is sweet natural gas. Estimated volume released is about 36,000 m³. The leak appears to be coming from the pipe body or a weld. Everything is contained within the station fence.

This station leaked back in 2022 too. No volume estimate yet.

Still investigating the source and cause.

Samantha Lee, Pipeline Patrol Contractor

report:
Got a gas leak at Rosetown station, found it at 0940 this morning. Sweet gas, approx. 24,000 m³ escaped. Looks like it's coming through the pipe body or maybe a weld. Haven't pinpointed it yet.

We had a leak here in 2023 too. Looks like it's coming from a flange on the meter run.

Contained inside the station fence. Shut down the line, venting to flare. Contractor crew's here now, starting repairs. Will update when we know more.

Dave
Area Supervisor, Aspen Ridge

The verbal and written notice together also satisfy the PIR (PIR-SAT).
Detailed Incident Report due within 84 days of the notification date (DIR-84).

The pipeline has been shut down, and the gas is being vented to the flare. A contractor crew is on-site and has begun repairs.
**PIR-9 Actions:** Shut down the line, venting to flare. Contractor crew's here now, starting repairs.

**PIR-11 Location:** Not stated in the field report.

**PIR-13 Nearest community:** Not stated in the field report.

**Reasons:**
- INC-e: Unintended or uncontrolled release of gas or HVP hydrocarbons
- PREC: When in doubt, notify: missing or disputed facts are taken at the reading that reports, at the earliest deadline
- T3-GAS30K: 3-hour notice: gas or HVP release over 30,000 m³
- DIR-84: Detailed Incident Report within 84 days of notification
